The board at the window

Everything's made when you order it.

The same short list it has always been: beef on the flat-top, cod in the fryer, curly fries out of the fryer. Tap a heading to see what's under it. Kids' meals still come in a cardboard 1957 Chevy.

On the wall inside

Opening day is painted on the wall inside.

The paper that week reported the crowd kept him busy all day, and that somebody claimed to have put away twenty-five cones.

That clipping hangs inside now, painted out at wall size. Local muralist Jamie Ferguson took the original announcement — the line of kids in ball caps, the ROOT BEER FLOAT sign, the PINEAPPLE SUNDAE sign — and put it on a panel; the current owners had it framed in a glossy retro moulding chosen to match the neon. It's worth looking up at while you wait.

The cod comes out of the fryer to order.

Out front and on the tray

A Saturday at the Freeze.

How it works

It's a walk-up window. No reservation.

  1. Park on Main

    Street parking runs right past the door. The lot beside the building is small, so most people grab a spot on the street and walk up.

  2. Order at the window

    Tell them what you want at the outside window. If it's cold out, they'll ask whether you'd rather sit inside.

  3. Take a table

    Red picnic tables and umbrellas out front. Booths, chrome chairs and the checkerboard floor in.
